#2017. Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

“I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a big call.”

“We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”

“It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is important. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”

“Obviously frustrated. The boys did everything to get the three points but it is gutting in the end. I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”

Raul Jimenez reacts after his late penalty saved a point for Wolves against Blackburn 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/aXvVeWw6fc

“Before the game we were predicting Wolves would be right up there [this season] and we thought it would be a comfortable win. But that was not the case.  Blackburn gave a really good account of themselves and had lots of openings. [Cesar] Peixoto will be breathing a massive sigh of relief with that handball.”

“Wolves got away with one if I am being really honest. In terms of their second-half performance, they did not do anywhere near enough. I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”

Bentley spills the corner but gets a free-kick. Moments later, the referee blows his whistle for the final time and the game ends level at 2-2. A dramatic opening night of the new Championship season at Molineux. If the Championship continues in this vein all season, it will be one hell of a year.

Blackburn nearly score a late winner as Garrett’s shot is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a later Blackburn corner.

He sends Toth the wrong way and calmly slots home to bring Wolves level in added time. That penalty decision will certainly create some debate. The Championship is always full of drama and we get some on opening night.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

It just had to be. Jimenez rescues Wolves from the penalty spot.

Drama on the opening night of the campaign.

Relief for Wolves, heartbreak for Blackburn.

Late drama at Molineux! The cross is sent in from the left and the ball strikes the arm Alebiosu on the edge of the box. Was it inside or outside the penalty area? It is definitely handball but was it outside the box? It was very, very close but there is no VAR in the Championship so the penalty will stand.

Four added minutes. Are we on the verge of seeing the first shock of the new Championship season on opening night?

Four minutes added. Not even a reaction from the home crowd.

Wolves are desperately running out of time and Blackburn still look comfortable.

Home fans are beginning to filter out slowly.

Mosquera is still struggling but he has come back on whilst limping around. I cannot imagine there will be too much in terms of added time, either three or four minutes would be my guess, no more.

Ohashi is played in behind and goes down under a challenge from Toti on the edge of the Wolves box but those appeals are waved away.

Mosquera has gone down again and he may not be able to continue as he receives treatment on the sidelines. Wolves may be ending this game down to 10 men.

Fevrier’s shot from outside the Wolves penalty area is blocked and spins behind for a corner in front of the travelling Blackburn fans. The corner comes to nothing.

Wolves struggling to create anything of note even with Jimenez’s introduction.

Centre-back Mosquera has gone up front but appears to be struggling with an injury. He’s jogged back to his natural position now.

Desperate long balls being sent forward but Blackburn look comfortable for now. The home fans are quite audibly unhappy with this second-half showing.

Wolves do not currently look like scoring an equaliser.

Mosquera is struggling with a knock but Wolves made all five changes. If he is unable to continue, Wolves will have to finish off with ten men.

The frustration inside Molineux is growing and the home fans want to see some more urgency from their side as they trail with under 10 minutes left.

Blackburn are now going to make their final two alterations of the night as Ribeiro and Garrett come on.

Wolves are going to make their final two substitutions as Lima and Chirewa replace Moller Wolfe and Andre.

Blackburn are looking pretty comfortable right now defending their lead and counter-attacking effectively.

Wolves want a penalty as Armstrong goes down inside the box after making a run in behind but the appeals are waved away. Rightly so as Armstrong was not fouled.

Wolves are pushing to find an equaliser but are struggling to carve out many genuine opportunities.

Ohashi is penalised for a foul on F Lopez not far outside the Blackburn penalty area and that was pretty harsh on Ohashi. Jimenez is lining this one up as is F Lopez.

The former takes but his effort hits the wall.

Wolves’ frustration right now is summed up by a dreadful cross from F Lopez from the right side of the box that goes behind for a goal kick. The TV cameras then turn to some of the Wolves fans, who look rather forlorn in the stands.

Double changes for both sides. For Wolves, Doyle and Tchatchoua come on. For Blackburn, Fevrier and Ohasi enter the fray.

You’d have thought a goal had gone in such is the reaction from the home crowd to Jimenez’s introduction. I have to say, I’m surprised Mane has made way but Jimenez will play through the middle with Armstrong moved out to the left.

Blackburn made a change earlier in the half with Wolverhampton-born Sam Morsy on for his Rovers debut. One manager going for it as the other attempts to shore things up.

Wolves’ last shot on target was all the way back in the 18th minute, when Munetsi put them in front. That is in fact their only shot on target tonight, compared to Blackburn’s four.

Should Wolves have been given a penalty? Jimenez goes down after Atcheson did stick out his leg but was there enough in it to give a penalty?

Jimenez is indeed now going to come on and Molineux rises to welcome him onto the pitch. The Jimenez scarfs go up around the ground and his song is sung. Mane goes off.

Raúl Jiménez receives an incredible reception from the Wolves fans as he makes his league return for the club 👏🇲🇽 pic.twitter.com/mPE7pvTJZt

No messing about from new Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto with his side behind and discontent brewing in the stands, Raul Jimenez is going to be introduced. His name has been sung throughout the game with a hero’s welcome imminent.

Can he inspire a comeback? Wolves and Peixoto will certainly hope so.

Munetsi, the scorer of Wolves’ goal, has a shot deflected from the edge of the box and it goes behind for a corner. Gudjohnsen, the scorer of Blackburn’s second, heads away at the front post.

You can sense the frustration growing from the home fans inside Molineux, with a few groans creeping in.

Blackburn are the first to turn to their bench as one experienced midfielder replaces another with Morsy coming on for Forshaw.

Wow! What a start to the second half. Blackburn have turned it around, Tony Mowbray clearly inspired his troops at half time.

Molineux is silenced now with Blackburn fans making all the noise. Some home supporters were still taking their seats as Gudjohnsen turned the ball home.

Can Wolves turn the game back in their favour? It’s all a bit slow now from the hosts followed by the first signs of disgruntlement from the home supporters.

And to top it off, Mane is booked for simulation.

The first Wolves player into the book tonight is Mane and it is for simulation. Watching the replays, that feels like a fair call as Mane threw himself to the ground and it probably was a dive.

Molineux is stunned as the underdogs take the lead inside the opening five minutes of the second half. Tony Mowbray’s side have started well since the break and are rewarded. Afolayan is found making a run into the penalty area on the right side of the box and his cross is slotted home by Gudjohnsen. His father Eidur would have been happy with a striker’s finish like that.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Morishita drives forward through the Wolves half and towards the penalty area. He lays it off to Afolayan, whose effort is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a Blackburn corner, which is headed and then cleared away by Wolves.

We are back under way at Molineux. No changes for either side at the break.

Possession: Wolves 52%-48% BlackburnShots: 10-4Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 3-2Touches in opposition box: 9-7

An intriguing first half as the whistle sounds and both teams head down the tunnel.

Both teams scored when the other seemed on top slightly.

Wolves have probably shaded it with those efforts from Lopez and Mane which went narrowly over.

Plenty to think about for the two managers.

The first half is brought to a close at Molineux and an engaging opening 45 minutes of the new Championship season results in this game being level at 1-1 at the break. Munetsi put Wolves in front before McLoughlin equalised for Blackburn.

Forshaw is the third Blackburn player into the book tonight as the referee goes back to penalise the midfielder for an earlier foul on Andre. That was not Forshaw’s first foul either.

With no VAR or hydration breaks, there will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Mane wins it back for his side on the edge of his own penalty area and drives forward. He takes it across the halfway line before feeding a lovely pass to his right to find Armstrong, whose shot is blocked.

Mane comes close to a stunner. Trippier rolls the ball across the face of the penalty area to 18-year-old Mane, who takes on the shot first time but his effort goes just over the bar.

Wolves come close to restoring their lead. Mane drives inside from the left and plays the ball forward to F Lopez, who takes one touch before getting his shot away from just outside the box. He tries to pick out the top corner but it just misses the target.

Like London buses, two yellow cards come at once and another Blackburn player is into the book. It is their captain Cantwell who receives a yellow card for delaying the restart. Cantwell was not too impressed with that decision.

Both teams off the mark for the season now, a brilliant near-post run and header from McLoughlin who scores his first-ever goal in English football to level the game up.

Molineux briefly stunned into silence. A slight delay from the fans celebrating the header as well.

The first booking of the Championship season goes the way of Blackburn left-back Pickering. It is a pretty simple decision for the referee as Pickering cynically pulls back R Gomes, who had spun him, and rightly receives a yellow card.

R Gomes delivers a cross from the right side of the Blackburn box across the penalty area but Armstrong does not pre-empt that and is not on hand to meet it. However, Alebiosu, with Mane not far behind him, puts it behind for a corner. Trippier delivers and the Blackburn keeper makes a meal of it, missing his punch out but then scrambles back towards his own goal to gather the loose ball.

The visitors went behind against the run of play but probably deservedly they are back on level terms. Morishita clips in the cross from the right to the near post, where McLoughlin meets it first and guides a powerful header into the far corner. Two goals in the opening half an hour of the new Championship season.

"They STUN Molineux!" 😳Sean Mcloughlin delightfully heads past Dan Bentley to equalise for Blackburn 👏 pic.twitter.com/v5qLhJ0wBt

Blackburn are getting great joy down their right through Alebiosu and Morishita, with the latter winning them a corner as Toti is forced to head behind from a cross. Pickering sends it into a good area and the touch comes off the head of Munetsi, whose header loops into the air and goes just over his own bar for another corner on the other side.

Cantwell’s delivery to the far post is headed away.

We have the first goal of the season and it’s the returning Marshall Munetsi who gets it.

A cool finish from the midfielder after a bit of a drab start from the home side.

That will please the new Wolves boss. Such a simple move but the home side ripped Blackburn wide open with two passes.

Work to do for the visitors now who had probably started the better of the two teams before the opener.

Wolves fans make their feelings about VAR known following the goal. No VAR in the Championship of course but no VAR was needed for that anyway. A perfectly good goal.

Mane cuts inside from the left onto his preferred right foot and curls a dangerous ball into the box that is punched away by Toth in the Blackburn goal. 18-year-old Mane was one of very few bright spots for Wolves last season and in many ways it is a surprise that no Premier League teams have lured him back to the top flight quite yet. That could though still happen before the deadline.

The first goal of the Championship season comes against the run of play. It is a clinical, ruthless goal that comes from an incisive pass and clinical finish. The pass is fed through by F Lopez to pick out the run of Munetsi, who is cool, calm and collected as he finishes past Toth. Blackburn had been the better side up until that point but Wolves take the lead at Molineux.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

A shot on target for Blackburn but an easy save in the end. Alebiosu, who has looked good in these early stages, drives down Blackburn’s right before cutting it back to Morishita on the edge of the box. Morishita takes one touch before shooting but his effort is tame and straight at Bentley.

Blackburn have definitely been the better side in these early exchanges, dominating possession and looking a threat going forward.

Blackburn may be heavy underdogs tonight but they have settled down well away at one of the favourites to get promoted. Tony Mowbray may well be seeing this as a good time to play Wolves away.

Alebiosu shows quick feet down Blackburn’s right and clips a cross to the back post, where Afolayan meets it but his header is just off target.

Safe to say the doom and gloom of last season appears to have lifted at Molineux. The home fans in fine voice early on here.

By contrast, Kieran Trippier’s first touch of the season is greeted by loud boos by the travelling Blackburn supporters.

In fact, every Trippier touch is greeted by a chorus of boos. Will they keep that up all game?

They’ve certainly not forgotten his Burnley connection.

New managers and new signings galore. This should be a fascinating spectacle.

He may not be in the starting XI tonight but Jimenez is being serenaded by the home fans on his return to Wolves after a few years away at Fulham. Jimenez and his wife have paid for 5,000 scarves for the Wolves fans tonight.

Blackburn boss Tony Mowbray did say ahead of the game that Wolves have not been used to winning games over the last 12 months so can the visitors take advantage of that tonight? Blackburn are underdogs tonight and not too much is expected of them this season so surely they have nothing to lose this evening?

Due to his Burnley ties, new Wolves defender Trippier is booed by the travelling Blackburn fans. On the other side of defence for Wolves is Moller Wolfe, who started for Norway against England in the World Cup quarter-finals in Miami.

After Jeff Beck’s Hi Ho Silver Lining rings around the stadium and tributes paid to former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes, we are under way at Molineux. The 2026/27 Championship season is officially under way.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off on opening night in the Championship.

When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager new to English football, it proved a vintage season.

Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the big question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

“I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

“There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”

Our experts have been having their say ahead of the new Championship season. A number of them believe Wolves will be promoted, including John Percy:

It is difficult to look beyond West Ham. Nuno Espírito Santo romped to the Championship title with Wolves in 2018 and remains a shrewd operator (along with his No 2 Rui Pedro Silva), while convincing Jarrod Bowen to stay is significant. I am going to go for Wolves and Middlesbrough as the other two promoted clubs.

The 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are new playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

Wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

“I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

“It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our big goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”

They have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

Blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

“I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray said. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”

These sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

#2016. Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham record as Arsenal teenager makes England history

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Max Dowman has added another incredible achievement to his burgeoning career after becoming the youngest player to play for the England Under-21s.

The Arsenal youngster was introduced from the bench in Friday’s 1-0 friendly loss to Portugal at Ashton Gate. The 16-year-10-month-13-day-old player is over three months younger than Jude Bellingham was when he played his first game for the Under-21s.

Dowman replaced former Arsenal academy player Amario Cozier-Duberry in the 61st minute. He came on alongside debutant Trey Nyoni as England tried to shift the momentum of a challenging game.

An early strike from Afonso Moreira gave Portugal the lead in the 28th minute. An ineffective England team failed to respond. However, the replacements gave Lee Carsley’s team some late momentum.

Despite the hosts’ attempts to level the score, they failed to break down the Portuguese defence. The result means England have lost for the second game running. However, Dowman had much to be pleased with personally.

Dowman has added to his growing collection of records.

He became the youngest player to play in the Champions League, the youngest goalscorer in the history of the Premier League and the youngest to win the Premier League title.

Breaking Bellingham’s England Under-21 record is another significant step. It shows how quickly Dowman has progressed through the international age groups.

He has already made a big impression at Arsenal with Mikel Arteta’s love of giving younger players a chance, but Dowman will have some stiff competition for first team minutes.

Another positive is his progression on an international scale. He will improve both physically and tactically playing against older players and gain experience at a higher level.

England will host France in their next friendly on Monday, 16th November. Dowman will be hoping to feature after his instant impact on the record books.

Despite the disappointing result against Portugal, it was a landmark evening for the Arsenal players.

Dowman is already building a legacy at club level, but now he can add to his list of records by becoming an England Under-21 record holder.

At just 16, he has plenty of time to improve and show consistent performances to get more opportunities with the senior Arsenal squad.

#2015. Chelsea sweat on key stars as Bournemouth test looms

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Chelsea return to Premier League action this weekend with a growing treatment table and a lot of questions for Xabi Alonso to answer before Saturday’s visit of Bournemouth.

The main concern revolves around Joao Pedro. Chelsea’s current player of the season rescued a point against newly promoted Hull, but he suffered a knock and sat out the damaging 3-0 defeat at Brentford. The problem also prompted his removal from Brazil’s squad shortly after he had returned to it.

It is understood that he is undergoing specialist knee treatment in an attempt to expedite his recovery, although reports in Brazil suggest that he could be out for up to four weeks. No date has yet been set, but a return later in October looks most likely.

There is more good news elsewhere. Cole Palmer was among the players called up to the latest England squad, which did not go down too well with Thomas Tuchel.

The midfielder has been recovering from a persistent groin injury and has been working with a rehab coach. He is likely to be fit this weekend.

Moises Caicedo has also struggled with an injury this season, playing just 14 minutes across the campaign. He’s spent the majority of time on the bench recovering from a bad calf injury, which ruled him out for most of the season.

He made his only appearance as a substitute against his former club Brighton, but the game was red-flagged for Ecuador’s friendlies, so he did not play.

Alonso said before the Brentford match that the player would be ready to return. It seems to be the case, unless something went wrong.

Captain Reece James missed the Brentford game with yet another hamstring problem. Alonso said he only just missed out, so a return seems likely.

There may also be debuts. Marco Palestra, the £27m signing from Atalanta, has been sidelined since a training injury just before the opening match against Fulham. He is back in full training and was expected to feature in a behind-closed-doors friendly with Portsmouth. Chelsea lost 2-0. Emmanuel Emegha, injured after scoring against Bromley in July, is also pushing for involvement.

Less clear is the position of Jamie Gittens. He limped off with an ankle injury playing for England Under-21s against Kazakhstan and was seen on crutches. Mike Penders is fine after a quad scare on Belgium duty. Returning to the bench against Turkey.

Chelsea badly need a lift. Defeat at Brentford before the break left Alonso’s side looking shaky, and a squad stretched by injuries has not helped.

Saturday brings a chance to steady things. If Palmer, James and Caicedo are available, with Palestra and Emegha potentially adding fresh options, the picture will look much brighter at Stamford Bridge. Joao Pedro’s absence will still sting. However, a strong response against Bournemouth would go a long way towards easing the pressure and restoring belief.

#2014. Discussions held with his agent: Liverpool could snap up ‘spectacular’ full-back for just £33m

According to one report, Liverpool have the opportunity to snap up a full-back from a fellow European giant for a modest amount.

The Reds have found a solution to the problematic right-back position with the loan acquisition of Ronald Araujo, who was originally signed to add centre-back cover but has excelled on the flank at Anfield.

Despite the Barcelona loanee’s fine form, Jamie Carragher has implored his former club to move for a full-back in January if the right opportunity arises, and there might just be another one from Camp Nou.

As reported by Graeme Bailey for TEAMtalk, the LaLiga champions are prepared to sanction an exit for Alejandro Balde amid interest from Liverpool, with Barca head coach Hansi Flick indicating that the 23-year-old isn’t part of his plans.

His representative Jorge Mendes has reportedly held talks with the Merseyside club to inform them of the conditions surrounding a potential deal for the player, who’s viewed by Anfield chiefs as an ‘attractive option’.

The agent is understood to have communicated a valuation of €40m (£33m) to prospective suitors, and that figure would apply whether the deal is structured as a permanent transfer or a loan arrangement with a purchase option.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Even though Balde has been overtaken by Xavi Espart and Joao Cancelo in the left-back pecking order at Barcelona, Liverpool might still feel that the price point apparently quoted by Mendes would represent something of a bargain for the 23-year-old.

Catalan columnist Javier Miguel has previously hailed some ‘spectacular’ performances from the Spain international (AS), and an analysis from The Athletic highlighted his aptitude for taking on opposition full-backs whilst marauding along the left flank.

He’s also renowned for his pace, with his former agent Junior Minguella describing him as a ‘bullet’, and Flick previously spoke of how the Spain international strives to ‘get better every day’ (The Athletic).

If Kostas Tsimikas were to depart at the end of his contract next summer – certainly not an implausible scenario – then Liverpool would need to add left-back competition for Milos Kerkez, and Barcelona’s apparent readiness to offload Balde could play into our hands.

Considering the success we’ve had so far with Araujo, FSG might just be inclined to sound out the Catalan giants about potentially adding another full-back option from Flick’s squad in 2027. This could be an intriguing one to watch over the coming months.

#2013. Martin Ødegaard sends clear message to Arsenal amid Bayern Munich transfer rumours

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Martin Ødegaard has spoken out about the speculation surrounding his future. He has stated he would like to stay at Arsenal for the future.

The captain has also admitted that talks about a new deal have not yet begun. Ødegaard is currently under contract until the summer of 2028. This leaves Arsenal with an important decision to make over the coming months.

Bayern Munich are being linked with an interest in the midfielder according to reports from Germany. The Bundesliga giants are said to be keeping their eyes on the player’s situation.

Speaking while on international duty with Norway, Ødegaard was quick to dismiss the speculation. He made it clear he is settled in north London and sees his future being at the Emirates Stadium.

There is no suggestion that the 27-year-old is seeking a move. Although comments do highlight a contract issue that Arsenal will be keen to resolve in the short term.

The Norwegian’s laid-back attitude should be encouraging for supporters.

He has made it clear that he is happy at the club and wants to stay here for the time being. This means that there is no need to panic.

However, Arsenal will have to get him to sign on the dotted line. Leaving his captain in the last year of his contract with no progress would cause an unnecessary distraction.

Since his permanent move from Real Madrid in 2021, Ødegaard has become a key player in Mikel Arteta’s plans. He has grown into a team leader and is one of the most influential players in the dressing room.

His importance has been shown by his inclusion in all 10 of Arsenal’s Premier League games so far this season. He has scored three goals.

This is a big improvement on last season, where he was hampered by injuries and failed to make much of an impact in front of goal.

It wouldn’t be a shock to see Bayern Munich show interest in Ødegaard, but don’t take this as a sign he is close to a move.

There is little reason for Arsenal to consider losing their captain. He brings so much more to the team than just his technical ability and has been relied upon by Arteta to lead by example.

The midfielder was also pivotal in the 1-0 win over Hull City on 7 November, scoring the winner in the 72nd minute to give the league leaders three crucial points.

Arsenal have put themselves in a good position in the title race. Keeping their key players happy will be important in the second half of the campaign.

The Gunners will be focused on their game against Newcastle United on 21st November.

Arsenal fans have no real reason to panic at the moment, with the captain wanting to stay at the club and his comments suggesting he is happy.

However, it would be a good idea for the club to try and ensure his long-term future at the club. Ødegaard is still an important part of Arteta’s strategy, and ensuring he stays at the club would be a smart move.

#2012. Chelsea co-sporting director Laurence Stewart to leave in leadership reshuffle

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

The departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

The changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not currently planning to recruit a replacement.

#2010. Arsenal Women held by London City Lionesses despite Frida Maanum goal

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women missed the chance to end their frustrating run of draws at home as London City Lionesses came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium.

Frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in an exciting start to the game. But Isobel Goodwin equalised almost straight away. Despite creating plenty of chances, Renée Slegers’ side failed to find a second goal.

Arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates. The results were yet another frustrating afternoon for the defending champions, who put in a strong display against Barcelona in Europe earlier in the week.

Arsenal started on a high note, creating some dangerous chances with their quick play. Emily Fox and Lisa Baum worked really well together down the right, and Ona Batlle had a great chance from the edge of the box.

As the pressure mounted, Fox surged forward and played a perfectly weighted through ball to Alessia Russo. The striker turned and played the ball back to Maanum, who rounded off her impressive comeback from injury by finishing.

Arsenal had little time to rejoice. London City equalised just a minute later as Goodwin found herself in space to fire past Misa Rodríguez.

The visitors looked more confident after equalising, but Mary Earps was proving a tough ask for Arsenal to score past. The ex-Manchester United shot-stopper kept out Baum and made some key stops from Arsenal’s efforts.

Rodriguez also had to make a key stop before half-time as she got a hand to Daniela Arques Lazaro’s powerful strike to keep the scores level.

The Gunners continued their attacking play but were made to work hard by a high pressing side from London City.

But Arsenal still managed to create some chances. Caitlin Foord put Earps under pressure and Maanum and Baum combined before the latter saw her curl just wide.

London City posed a threat too. With Kadidiatou Diani and Grace Geyoro causing defensive problems for Arsenal, Geyoro fired into the side netting.

Delphine Cascarino had the game’s defining moment of the second half, hitting the crossbar from outside the box. However, Arsenal were lucky to escape and Maanum came close to winning the game, hitting the woodwork from a dangerous counter.

Slegers brought on Kyra Cooney-Cross and Olivia Smith in the 72nd minute to provide some new energy. Smith looked lively upon entering the game, but Earps denied her efforts and Batlle’s cross.

Emily Fox had to be substituted due to injury in the final moments of the game, but Slegers later indicated that she would be okay.

The Gunners were unable to find a winning goal and will now turn their attention to their Champions League clash on Thursday with Lyon. They will then face West Ham at home in the WSL.

Bournemouth’s determination to keep Alex Scott has done little to discourage Chelsea, who remain among the leading contenders to sign the England midfielder.

Bournemouth, however, have no intention of allowing Scott to leave in January. talkSPORT reported this week that the south coast club remain determined to retain him, despite his reluctance to sign a contract extension.

Scott’s current deal runs until 2028, leaving Bournemouth with time to negotiate, although their position could become more complicated if no agreement is reached before next summer.

The midfielder’s immediate priority is recovering from a thigh injury sustained while representing England. His absence is a setback for Bournemouth, who have relied heavily on the former Bristol City midfielder this season. It also introduces another consideration for clubs monitoring his progress ahead of the January window.

Chelsea are not alone in their admiration. Arsenal and Liverpool have also been linked with Scott, whose performances have attracted attention beyond the Premier League.

Suggestions circulating on social media that Bournemouth have already agreed to let him leave in January remain unsubstantiated. There has been no reliable confirmation of such an arrangement, and the club’s reported position is firmly against a winter sale.

#2008. Declan Rice’s latest Arsenal evolution shows why Arteta wanted him tied down

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Declan Rice’s new contract shows how much of an asset he is to Mikel Arteta. His recent performances show why.

The England international has reportedly signed a new five-year deal which will keep him at the Emirates Stadium until 2031. The contract is a reward for the midfielder who has been instrumental in Arsenal’s success since he moved to the club in 2023 from West Ham.

Rice has not just provided the presence and protection that Arsenal were hoping for with their £105 million signing. He has continued to develop his game, especially after returning to his deeper midfield role this season.

Rice came in as a defensive midfielder, but Arteta quickly saw how much he could offer higher up the park.

His physicality, ability to run into the box and set piece threat made him a useful left-sided number eight. Rice had a huge impact in midfield for Arsenal, bringing goals and a new attacking threat.

But Rice has played in a more advanced position on the right-hand side of the midfield duo this season, and this has not limited his impact but instead highlighted another key part of his game.

Rice has made the most line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season, with Opta stats reported by Sky Sports showing he is second only to Premier League players.

This is of particular interest, as he has often come under criticism for his distribution. But he is averaging nearly double the amount of line-breaking passes he did last season.

While his running ability is still an asset, he is also becoming much better at penetrating through the defensive lines to find his teammates, giving Arsenal another option to move the ball forward with.

The development of Rice is key in securing a new contract at Arsenal.

The 27-year-old has already proven to be one of the most reliable members of Arteta’s squad and has shown great longevity by only missing five games out of his 119 Premier League outings in his first spell at the club.

Former West Ham teammate Jack Wilshere has also praised Rice’s strong work ethic, ability to adapt and natural leadership qualities.

The reported 5-year deal will keep Rice at Arsenal until 2031, into his early 30s. While the terms of the deal have yet to be signed, it is a huge statement from the club.

They are not only rewarding Rice for what he has done but also investing in what he can do.

With Arteta finding new ways to utilise Rice’s qualities in midfield, Rice could still have some of his best years ahead of him.

#2007. Martin Zubimendi sends fresh Arsenal message as January transfer speculation grows

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Martin Zubimendi has raised questions among Arsenal fans over his future. This follows comments from the midfielder that he is keen to succeed in north London despite struggling for game time this season.

The Spain international has been linked with a move to Chelsea, Atletico Madrid and Real Madrid ahead of the January transfer window. Reports from Spain have said that Zubimendi’s situation at the club is becoming more complex, with the player possibly being available.

Zubimendi has also spoken about the speculation. In his interview during the international break with Marca, he said he did not feel like he was near to a move to Atletico, and he is still delighted to be in London.

He added the 27-year-old has had no contact with any other clubs. His priority is to get into Arteta’s squad.

This is an interesting response to the transfer speculation that has been building. Arsenal may well attract interest for one of their midfielders. However, there does not appear to be any evidence that Zubimendi is actively looking to leave.

In his first season, he played 38 times in the Premier League and became an important member of Arteta’s midfield. However, he has not started a league game this season.

Opta Analyst shows that he has only played 100 minutes in the Premier League in seven games. He has also faced increased competition for a spot in the team with the arrival of Bruno Guimarães.

Myles Lewis-Skelly is also an option in the middle of the park. Zubimendi will have to fight for his place back.

It is understood Arteta had a chat with Zubimendi ahead of the campaign and made it clear he would face more competition from the new signings and would have to earn his place.

Zubimendi has accepted the challenge and has said he could see it as a chance to learn and improve due to his reduced workload.

The interest from Spain and Chelsea will make it a tough choice if the right offers come in. However, losing Zubimendi will mean Arteta won’t have as many options to call upon in the busy second half of the season.

But he proved his worth in the game against Slavia Prague earlier this month. He started the Champions League match and played the full 90 minutes.

This shows that his contribution shouldn’t be judged purely on how much he plays in the Premier League. Arsenal will have a busy schedule in Europe and domestically, and he may provide some much-needed quality in the midfield.

With Zubimendi contracted until 2030, there is no immediate reason for Arsenal to look to sell him. He will have time to fight for his spot in the starting XI.

Despite not making a commitment to remain at the club beyond January, his remarks indicate that he is not on the lookout for alternatives.

The priority for Arsenal will be trying to find a way to get the best out of Zubimendi. He was a regular last season and seems happy to wait for his chance.

Chelsea have reportedly made contact with Palmeiras as they attempt to gain an early advantage in the race to sign Brazilian teenager Eduardo Conceicao.

Chelsea have already demonstrated their willingness to agree deals for young players well before they are eligible to arrive, with Estevao providing a particularly relevant example.

#2005. Liverpool have no excuses not to sign Ronald Araujo permanently as Deco leaves the door wide open

Barcelona sporting director Deco has left the door wide open for Liverpool to sign Ronald Araujo permanently.

The Uruguayan joined the Reds on a season-long loan in August and has made an immediate impression on the Anfield faithful, putting in a series of tremendous performances at right-back for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Reports from Spain in recent days have indicated that Merseyside chiefs are keen to take up the option to sign the defender outright for £47m, with the player also understood to be ready to stay in L4 beyond next summer.

Liverpool’s chances of securing him on a permanent basis would appear to have been greatly boosted by comments from Deco.

The Barcelona chief told Catalunya Radio’s Tot Costa: “A bit of money wouldn’t hurt us either. We’d be happy because things have gone well, and we’d be happy for him too.

“Personally, I’m happy for Ronald. He’s one of the team’s leaders. He’s been through some difficult times and some happy ones at the club, and we have a good relationship.

“He’s made his decision, and we respect it. The most important thing for us is to see him happy. If he decides to stay and things carry on like this, we’d be happy with that too.”

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

It seems that, if Liverpool were to sign Araujo permanently, everyone would be a winner.

The Reds would secure a player who’s been excellent for them (and get a deal done at a relatively modest fee), the defender would get to remain on Merseyside (where his family are reportedly very happy), and Barcelona would bank nearly £50m for someone they’re seemingly happy to let go.

Even with Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni finally back in first-team training, both of them will realistically need a few more weeks to be properly matchday ready, so Iraola will continue to depend heavily on the Uruguayan to maintain form and fitness.

Liverpool won’t be able to activate the purchase option on Araujo until the end of the season, and it’s not implausible that he could succumb to a serious injury or see his performance levels drop in the meantime.

Right now, though, there’s no excuse for Anfield chiefs not to go all-out to secure a permanent transfer, especially with Deco indicating that Barcelona would be prepared to sanction his sale. Don’t fumble this one please, Julian Ward!

Chelsea’s sporting department is facing another change following news of Laurence Stewart’s impending departure, while the club continue to be linked with potential additions to their squad.

Here is our 7pm round-up of the latest Chelsea news for Thursday, 8 October.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club planning to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

Our Chelsea v Bournemouth kick-off and how-to-watch guide provides the full details, including how to follow the match and the available overseas broadcast information.

Scott’s injury is expected to deprive Bournemouth of an important midfield option, although Chelsea will have their own fitness decisions to make as players return from international duty.

After Saturday’s fixture, Chelsea travel to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton on 17 October. Alonso will be looking for greater consistency as the domestic programme resumes.

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Viktor Gyökeres is reminding Arsenal of his prolific goal scoring capabilities.

The striker found the back of the net twice in Sweden’s 3-2 Nations League win against Bosnia and Herzegovina on November 14, both times from the spot to take his total to four in the Nations League this season.

The win also means they have booked their place in League A with one match left to play in the group, and Gyökeres has certainly played his part in this excellent run.

However, the performance will raise questions about his future at the club. The idea that he may be leaving in January is a possibility that needs to be looked at.

There is a stark difference between his international and club form.

Gyökeres has only played 181 minutes in seven Premier League games this season, starting just once as Kai Havertz has usually been preferred in central areas.

However, he has had more opportunities to play in European competition. Gyökeres has started three of Arsenal’s four matches in the Champions League, scoring one goal and providing two assists.

Gyökeres is not totally out of Arteta’s plans, but he will not play much domestically.

He has been in fine form internationally recently. Sweden are building their attack around his movement and penalty area presence, meaning he will have chances to regularly perform.

However, just because he is doing well internationally does not mean he will start regularly for the club. Arteta has other attacking options and tactics to consider.

There have been suggestions surrounding Gyökeres’ future, with reports that Arsenal may look to add more attacking flair to their squad.

AC Milan and Juventus have also been linked, but there is no agreement or suggestion that either club is looking to make a January move for the forward.

Gyökeres has opened up about the speculation.

In an interview with Swedish media outlet Fotbollskanalen during the international break, he stated that he would like to stay at the club. The player also denied any issues with his relationship with Arteta, stating that they have good communication.

However, the player may not stay forever, as he has not played much in the Premier League so far. If this continues, and Arsenal sign another forward, it could cause an issue.

For now, though, there is little evidence that Gyökeres is trying to leave the club.

He’ll be looking to get regular game time at 28 after finding his scoring touch with Sweden. Arsenal will also need to work out how to use him best as a goalscoring striker.

But for now the January speculation seems a little early. He has stated he wants to stay at Arsenal, and the next few weeks may prove to be more important.

#2000. Arsenal mourns Peter Storey: 1971 Double-winning hero dies aged 81

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

Storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

He was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

Storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

Storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

Storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

He played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

Following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

He will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

#1999. Liverpool sending scouts ‘every week’ to watch red-hot sensation in shock Golden Boot contention

According to reports from Italy, Liverpool are regularly scouting a red-hot striker who’s emerged as a shock candidate for the Golden Boot in Serie A this season.

Andoni Iraola has been almost exclusively reliant on Alexander Isak at centre-forward since taking charge of the Reds in the summer, with Hugo Ekitike continuing his recovery from a long-term Achilles injury.

The Frenchman is targeting a return to action next month (The Athletic), although it appears that Anfield chiefs are keeping tabs on a positional alternative who’s emerging as a breakthrough sensation in one of Europe’s major leagues.

A report from Corriere dello Sport has claimed that Liverpool are sending scouts ‘every week’ to watch Gustavo Varela, who’s been in remarkable goalscoring form with Monza since joining the Serie A outfit in the summer.

Napoli and Juventus have also been strongly linked with the 21-year-old, who’s been the subject of enquiries from Tottenham, Brentford and Sunderland, with the list of suitors growing in tandem with his goal return in the Italian top flight.

Ivan Juric’s side reportedly want €40m (£33.5m) for the Portuguese hitman, which’d represent a monumental profit on a player they signed from Gil Vicente in July for a paltry €2.5m (£2.1m).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Varela is currently the leading scorer in Serie A this season with nine goals, which is remarkable when his team are currently in the relegation zone, and he accounts for more than half of their goal tally in the top flight so far.

For someone who’d scored just seven times in 34 senior appearances before the summer, his form since joining Monza has been extraordinary. Should that continue, it’s safe to say that he won’t be at the Stadio Brianteo for much longer.

What Liverpool would need to consider is whether this is a mere purple patch from the Portuguese youngster, or the start of a journey towards being one of Europe’s most feared centre-forwards.

Varela has scored nine Serie A goals from an xG of just 5.48 (Fotmob), an astonishing overperformance which begs the question as to whether he can maintain that for a full campaign.

If Isak keeps up his own hot streak and Ekitike gets back to the levels he’d shown prior to his injury, it’d be difficult to see the Monza striker getting much of a look-in at Anfield.

However, it’s easy to see why Liverpool are routinely dispatching scouts to gather information on one of the breakout stars of European football in 2026.

Winger Christos Tzolis wants to prove he has a lot to offer Arsenal beyond his attacking prowess.

Since making his debut for the club, Tzolis has become a more rounded attacking threat. He has started all 7 Premier League games this season and provides a reliable option on the left for Arteta.

Scott would add quality in midfield, and Paz adds creativity and versatility going forward. Arteta must consider that adding these players may hinder the development of current players.

Arsenal are believed to be keen on bringing Alex Scott to the club.

After rejecting contract offers from Bournemouth, Scott could only have one year left on his contract at the club next summer. However, he is understood to be valued by Bournemouth at over £100m.

He would be a great addition for Arteta, with the versatility and skill he has. He could give added competition in midfield.

Yet his potential arrival raises questions about Myles Lewis-Skelly’s future role.

Myles Lewis-Skelly was included in the Champions League final line-up last season. He showed that he is trusted by the club.He has also demonstrated his commitment by remaining at the club despite opportunities to gain regular playing time at other clubs.

Signing another expensive midfielder may present difficulties. It is unclear at this point whether Scott will be a useful addition to the squad or simply overcrowd this area of the team.

Nico Paz presents another interesting option for Arsenal.

Paz joined Como from Real Madrid in the summer. He has caught the eye of a number of big clubs and has increased his appeal with strong performances in international football. The 22-year-old has scored 5 times in his last 5 games for Argentina.

Paz is a versatile right-sided player and could be an appealing addition to Arteta’s strike force.

There are already plenty of players fighting for attacking positions at Arsenal.

Bukayo Saka is key in the team’s attack, and with Martin Ødegaard and Noni Madueke in the squad too, there are plenty of options. Max Dowman is a young player looking to break into the first team.

While Paz would add quality to the squad, Arsenal would need to find a specific role for him. There are complications with the move, though. Real Madrid have an option to re-sign him in 2027 for 80 million euros.

Although Arsenal are facing challenges in attracting quality players to the club. They now also face issues in managing a squad with experienced internationals and developing young players.

Although Scott and Paz would improve the depth of the squad, players must not be sacrificed for new players if they have already shown quality.

Players such as Lewis-Skelly and Dowman may be negatively affected by this. Opportunities may be taken away from them if the club continues to spend large amounts of money on new players.

However, it is still very important for Arsenal to bring in quality players to compete for major titles.

Know how the additions will integrate within the playing style and how they affect the other players within the squad.

The Gunners can strengthen further without overloading the squad. Good additions can be made to the first XI whilst also providing a realistic chance for young players to come through from within the academy.

#1993. Max Dowman’s Arsenal return: Is the teenage star one to watch, and can he keep his nose clean?

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Max Dowman shortly returns to action for Arsenal after serving a three-game suspension.

His absence has been disappointing, but the experience should give the youngster an important lesson. Can he put the incident behind him and show Mikel Arteta that he can be trusted?

Dowman received a red card against Fleetwood Town after kicking out at Harrison Neal. Arsenal appealed the decision, but the FA rejected the club’s appeal.

The suspension ruled him out of three domestic fixtures against Liverpool, Hull City and Newcastle United.

He’ll be back on 29 November as Arsenal take on Manchester City. This should give the young star a chance to get his season back on track and showcase what makes him such a highly-rated player.

Dowman looks very promising for the future. He has shown great adaptability playing with the more experienced players and has the self-belief to make an impact in games.

He has performed well in the Carabao Cup. In the 4-2 win against Ipswich, Dowman scored two goals, showing his flair and poise in front of goal.

Arteta has given him opportunities to play in the Premier League and Champions League, meaning that he appears to have a clear route into the first team.

Although Dowman still has a lot to learn, he displays great potential in his technical ability and combative nature. As he gets more games under his belt, fans will be excited to see how he progresses.

Dowman was sent off in an unfortunate moment. He was heavily challenged by Neal and, after lashing out, was shown a straight red card.

Although this one moment should not be enough to dismiss a young player from the game completely, it can serve as a valuable lesson on the pressure that comes with playing at a higher level.

Opponents will test Dowman physically, but he must learn to keep his composure. As he starts making an impact, some players may target his age and inexperience to unsettle him.

As he gets more game time, consistency will be key. Arteta must be confident that Dowman can be relied on in high pressure situations.

Arsenal do not need to rush Dowman into the first team. The squad’s quality allows Arteta to manage his minutes and give him time to develop without putting too much pressure on him.

If Dowman is to play against Manchester City, it will depend on Arteta’s plans, but he has certainly done enough to warrant consideration.

The suspension should not define his season. What matters now is how he responds, both on and off the pitch.

Dowman has the talent to become an important player for Arsenal. Keeping his discipline will be just as important as displaying his ability.

#1992. Former West Ham talisman finally gets his dream trophy after quitting east London

The manner in which some players depart West Ham along with the bad feeling that develops as they press for a departure on their own terms can sometimes be the lasting memory that tarnishes their whole stay in east London.

Such was certainly the case of Marco Arnautovic, for example, a successful forward who demanded a new deal, got everything he wanted, and then quit anyway.

However, with some players, despite the bitterness, the rancorous ending of their career fades in the memory over time, and their stay is regarded more fondly for the highlights rather than the bad blood generated at the close.

Not quite sure yet which category the career and departure of Lucas Paqueta will fit into as his stay at West Ham thankfully fades into the dim and distant past.

Infuriating, gifted, inconsistent, yes, but forever remembered for ‘that’ pass to Jarrod Bowen in June 2023, Paqueta’s ‘yellow cards for bets‘ two year saga became, sadly, the other defining memory of his three years as a Hammer.

Winning the conference League title was his career pinnacle – until last weekend when he finally achieved ‘the ambition of a lifetime‘  (huh) with his boyhood club Flamengo.

Looking on the bright side, West Ham fans don’t have to endure the ‘baggage’ that came with Lucas Paquetá

As reported by sportwitness.co.uk, West Ham’s former number ten referred merely to his time in England as ‘two very difficult years’ en route to winning the Brazilian league title:

““I went through two very difficult years in my life. I decided to come back because I wanted this feeling, I wanted to feel welcomed, to be at the club I love.”

“I have no words to describe what I’m feeling. I arrived at this club when I was eight years old. My biggest dream was always to win trophies wearing this shirt.”

Well done, Lucas. We’re all very happy for you.

It feels a bit like learning an ‘ex’ has got remarried. Good for them. So what? I’m so over them now…

#1990. Arsenal transfer news: Why Kevin Schade could be a smart January signing

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are looking to strengthen their attacking options in January. One player they are reportedly keeping an eye on is Brentford winger Kevin Schade. Mikel Arteta will be keen to add competition in attack, and Schade may be a good option.

Schade will give additional pace to the offence. He is capable of playing in multiple attacking positions to provide Arteta with extra depth in the squad.

However, it may be difficult to get Schade. He is on loan at Brentford, and may want to keep him in the long term. If Schade is seen as a key player in the future, they may be difficult to negotiate with.

Schade’s versatility is another big plus. His speed and straightforward method make him hard to deal with for defenders. In addition, he can be used as a left-sided attacker, giving Arteta more flexibility in his front line. As the club are playing in a number of competitions, this can be very useful.

Schade has already scored 3 times in the Premier League this season. He has quickly adapted to playing in England after moving from Freiburg to Brentford in 2023.

Despite only being 24 years old, Schade still has a lot to improve on. He has lots of experience in the Premier League but has not quite reached the peak of his ability yet. If he moves to Arsenal, he may be able to elevate his performance.

Brentford has already started negotiations with Schade regarding a contract extension that would keep him tied to the club for a long time. He is already contracted until the summer of 2028.

Arsenal’s interest could prove problematic. Other clubs are also keeping their eyes on this player. Tottenham in particular are not seen as a major threat at this stage.

It is going to be very challenging for Brentford to let go of Schade because he has played a key part in their offensive setup, and losing Schade could prove disastrous.

Arsenal will have to pay Brentford whatever they ask for, Schade, and since he has a decent amount of time left on his contract, Brentford has an edge in negotiations.

Arsenal’s interest in Schade is logical. His versatility will provide Arteta with additional flexibility because of his prior experience in the Premier League.

It can be considered positive to sign new strikers. Arsenal must decide if they believe that Schade will fit in well with their current players and whether the asking price from Brentford is reasonable.

As of now, there are no signs of a transfer on the horizon, but it is clear that Schade is a player worth monitoring as the winter transfer window approaches.
