#1970. Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand said everything you need to know about this moment...

Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town

Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City

United’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

Four minutes of added time to be played...

United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

Martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

More substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

Big chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

Milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

More changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by new signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

Milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

United have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

All square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

Fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

Santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs

United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

Shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

Carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

Estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

Milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

United make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

Szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

The players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely new cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

We are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

Manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

Marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

Carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

In memory of Franco Baresi 🇮🇹♾️ pic.twitter.com/ULAJRjxDvE

Manchester United Lammens; Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Tielemans, Santos, Fernandes; Amad, Dorgu; Cunha

Subs Heath, Mee, Amass, Dalot, Martínez, Yoro, Collyer, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Mainoo, Gabriel, Lacey, Mbeumo, Rashford, Zirkzee

AC Milan Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlović; Chukwueze, Jashari, Musah, Estupiñán; Loftus-Cheek, Cissè; Ramos

Subs Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Diawara, Vladimirov, Ricci, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Modrić, Comotto, Camarda

At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

“It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

“But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

“Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”

Aug 1: Manchester United 2 Atlético Madrid 1

Aug 8: Paris St-Germain 1 Manchester United 1

Aug 12: Manchester United 1 Leeds United 1 (5-4 pens)

Gonçalo Ramos goes straight into Amorim’s starting XI after his switch from PSG.

Our starting XI is set 🔒 pic.twitter.com/Qqo19UTCb4

New signing Youri Tielemans handed first start as one of six changes to the XI that faced Leeds United.

Our final starting XI of Tour 2026! 📋🤍ℹ️ Squad numbers worn in pre-season are provisional and yet to be finalised.

Welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri said Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

Carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, new signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

#1969. Embarrassing Didi Hamann comments on Newcastle United

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Didi Hamann has been talking about Newcastle United.

Didi Hamann signed for Newcastle United in 1998 from Bayern Munich.

Kenny Dalglish the United manager who signed him for a reported £5.5m fee after the 1998 World Cup finals where he’d played for Germany.

Didi Hamann now giving his opinion on Newcastle United’s future stadium plans…

The former player turned pundit asked by Lottoland Live Casino: ‘Newcastle United are reportedly yet to decide whether to renovate or expand St James’ Park or build a completely new stadium. Do Newcastle United need a completely new stadium?’

Didi Hamann replying: “No, no, you can’t leave St James’ Park. Obviously, I was fortunate and lucky to be able to play there for one season. I think it’s one of the best grounds in the league. With the extension they had, I think they get 51,000 [ED: 52k+ capacity now], and they probably can fit a few more in. If they can extend it, I think they’ve got to do everything to keep it. It’s right in the middle of the city. I think it’s one of the best, one of the most iconic stadia in the world. And I think this is why it would be majorly important to keep St James’. Don’t leave St James’ Park, please.”

It is embarrassing that Didi Hamann is passing comment on this, considering how he was so desperate to leave St James’ Park less than a year after arriving and move to Liverpool.

The German international only started 20 Premier League matches for Newcastle United before forcing his way out of the club. In total he started 30 competitive games for United, plus one sub appearance. So fair to say he will have only started around 15 games in total at St James’ Park in a Newcastle United shirt.

The other thing when you are commenting on a club you don’t really care about, is that you also know precious little about the subject matter. If Didi Hamann had done his research then he would have known that there are zero plans to move the home of Newcastle United out of the city centre. That if indeed there is a new stadium built, then it will go up on a site no more than hundreds of yards away, very possibly even partly on the current St James’ Park site.

The former (very short-term!) United star also asked: ‘Newcastle and Liverpool are both known for their incredible atmospheres. Having played at both grounds, which stadium do you think has the better atmosphere and where did you enjoy playing more?’

Didi Hamann: “It’s very hard to compare because we didn’t play in Europe with Newcastle. Obviously, European nights at Anfield have always been special. But I’ve got to say, to walk out the first time at St James’ was just electric. When the music comes on, when you walk out and you see in my time, I think it was about 40, 45,000 Geordies [Ed: SJP capacity was 36k+ then] there. It was just fantastic. At the same time, I was in awe when I played with Newcastle the first time. I think it was Boxing Day that season in 1998 when we played Liverpool. When you stand in the tunnel there before it got redone. I think they are two of the best stadia in England. I’d go Premier League games at Newcastle, European nights at Anfield.”

#1968. Are The Inbetweeners at Newcastle United capable of showing they deserve another series?

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

The Inbetweeners at Newcastle United, can they become success stories this series (this season) and beyond.

So much could depend on how this quarter perform.

Just in case you weren’t aware, The Inbetweeners is a brilliant (in my opinion anyway) comedy series (that has also then produced a couple of excellent films).

This comedy is the story of four teenagers who are misfits, neither totally cool nor total outcasts (hence The Inbetweeners), who regularly find themselves in awkward situations of their own making,

This fictional quartet occasionally hint of moving on to a consistently successful level, but their own inherent frailties as well as outside factors, time after time conspire to prevent those glimpses of promise becoming ever more than that.

My focus isn’t on individuals who have just arrived this summer at St James’ Park, it isn’t on young players, it isn’t on older players where we pretty much know what we are going to get.

When it comes to The Inbetweeners at Newcastle United, I wanted to concentrate on this quartet below.

Four players who have played plenty of Premier League football in their careers and have shown enough to suggest they COULD be important, indeed vital, for Newcastle United this season.

All four of them also happen to play in the key midfield and attacking positions, the positions where United need far higher input and productivity if they are to create the chances and score the goals that can make the (positive) difference this season.

So without further ado, here are The Inbetweeners at St James’ Park:

I think that arguably he is THE ultimate Inbetweener at Newcastle United. He was brilliant in that 2022-23 fourth place finish season before then serious injury hit then fitness and form issues have followed.

At times we see THAT Joe Willock of 2022-23 and the second half on Saturday a prime example. Against his former club he was the key man in that second half,  the pressing of opposition players and his running with the ball, the Arsenal midfield couldn’t handle him at times. Willock pressured Odegaard into the mistake that produced the equaliser and then an assist for Thiaw’s strike.

Joe Willock would deserve to be first name on the team sheet if he consistently played like he did in that second half.

Started the season in electric form, confidence sky high as he scored within five minutes of the opening game against Liverpool, then in the first EPL away game scored a brilliant goal to set United on their way to beating Spurs.

Then injury hit and when he has returned, it feels a bit like Snakes and Ladders. He climbed plenty of ladders and got into a great position brimming with confidence, he then though hits one snake that sends his confidence and form sliding right back to rock bottom and needing to start again.

I bit like Willock and Saturday’s second half, Elanga needs to simply get his head back in the place it was when Liverpool and Spurs couldn’t handle him. He is capable of being a huge player for Matthias Jaissle AND he needs to be that player to solve our problem on the right. He did alright on Saturday when he came on and maybe a huge factor can be if Tino Livramento now can stay fit as well on that side.

Very similar story to Anthony Elanga, started this season on fire and then lost his way.

In certain moments, Yoane Wissa has looked unplayable (in a good way!) this season, some of his runs on the ball have been exhilarating. The one he made with a handful of Liverpool players challenging him half the length of the pitch before passing to Joe Willock for his goal, where has that gone?

Again like Elanga, with Wissa it feels like it is very much a confidence thing.

He had an astonishing record at Brentford but I do feel he is an attacker who is more of a team player, he needs those around him also playing well. Hopefully if the team overall can become more consistent and then Yoane Wissa finds within that some special moments of his own, we can just maybe have that opening of this season player back again.

Of this quartet of Inbetweeners at Newcastle United, I think Ramsey deserves to be cut the most slack.

The former Villa star has still only started 15 Premier League matches for Newcastle United and was very unlucky with a bad early injury last season (thanks to Sean Longstaff) and desperately needs a run in the team to get his rhythm after having his own struggles with fitness and form.

Like the other three above, Jacob Ramsey has had moments where we can see the player Eddie Howe signed. The same as Joe Willock, Ramsey is very mobile, runs well with the ball, can be very effective with a high press, can be a difference maker.

The second half on Saturday he showed that and I do think that if Newcastle United are to exceed any current expectations, we need to have players with pace who can quickly carry the ball in transition an cause problems for opposition teams on a regular basis. If Jacob Ramsey and Joe Willock can do it against the best team in the country, admittedly just for one half on Saturday, why can’t they do it against the rest?

Once again though, the same as Yoane Wissa and Anthony Elanga, it is all about this quarter losing their status as The Inbetweeners at Newcastle United and proving to be something far better than that.

Here’s hoping they prove they are worthy of another series.

#1967. After tempted away from West Ham, highly rated teenager signs professional contract with Newcastle United

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Back in July, Kyle Healy-Matthews was tempted away from West Ham by Newcastle United.

The highly teenage starlet was a young player the Hammers were desperate not to lose.

Newcastle United fighting off a number of other Premier League clubs who had been competing to attract the teenage right-back.

However, personal terms were agreed between NUFC and Kyle Healy-Matthews and the deal completed

Obviously one for the future he looked a very positive addition, the young right-back is quick and with very good defensive ability, he’d been a stand out player in the West Ham young set-up.

Since the October 2021 takeover, Newcastle United having signed a lot of promising young players from other clubs, which will hopefully pay longer-term benefits.

Now Newcastle United have revealed on Wednesday morning that Kyle Healy-Matthews has signed his first professional contract with the club on his 17th birthday.

Official Newcastle United media stating: ‘The Romford-born youngster joined Newcastle’s Academy from West Ham United last summer and initially linked up with Chris Moore’s Under-18s squad as a first-year scholar before agreeing professional terms with the Magpies. Healy-Matthews, who primarily plays as a right-back, expressed his delight in committing his future with Newcastle and has relished his time at United’s Little Benton Academy to date.’

Kyle Healy-Matthews: “I’m very pleased to sign my first professional contract,” he told newcastleunited.com. “It’s a special moment for myself and my family, seeing all the hard work which has led up to this. Newcastle is a massive club with goals and ambitions that I feel I can contribute in. I believe I can play a big part for this club. I’ve enjoyed my time here a lot. I’ve had a lot of support from my peers and coaches with helping me to settle in as well as progressing along the way.”

The official NUFC media going on to say: ‘Kyle Healy-Matthews, who cites fellow right-back Kyle Walker as his footballing idol, has made a positive start to the current campaign at Under-18 level, with the Toon teenagers winning six of their opening seven league matches and currently occupying third spot in the division. The rapid full-back believes he has handled the challenge of relocating hundreds of miles away from home for the first time and is determined to advance through the Magpies’ youth ranks. Healy-Matthews, a member of West Ham’s Under-17 Premier League Cup winning side last season.’

Kyle Healy-Matthews: “I’ve only been here for a few months but I think I can say the move has paid off. Moving very far away from home could have been tricky but with all of the support I had around me from my peers, that really helped me to settle in quickly. I’m loving my time with the Under-18s. This season, my main aim is to progress into the Under-21s and long-term, but hopefully not too long, would be to progress into the first-team.”

Steve Harper is Newcastle United Academy Director: “Kyle has made an excellent impression since joining the Academy in the summer and we’re pleased to see him rewarded with his first professional contract. Moving away from home and settling into a new environment can be a significant challenge for any young player but Kyle has handled the transition brilliantly. He’s worked extremely hard since arriving at the club and his attitude, commitment and willingness to learn have stood out throughout his time here so far. This contract is recognition of the progress he’s made, and we’re excited to continue supporting his development as he takes the next steps in his career at Newcastle United.”

#1966. Liverpool games v Man United and Everton moved as Premier League confirm updated fixture details

Two more Liverpool fixtures in the Premier League have been rescheduled for live TV coverage, as confirmed on Thursday.

With the November international break now concluded, the Reds’ next couple of domestic fixtures are against Manchester United and Everton, with the reverse of those games against our two biggest traditional rivals taking place on consecutive weekends in January.

The fixture list for the remainder of this year had already been locked in, and the first month of 2027 has now been set, other than prospective FA Cup and Carabao Cup matches.

On Thursday, the Premier League announced updated dates and times for matches in January, with two of Liverpool’s games being moved.

The home clash against Crystal Palace remains a 3pm kick-off on Saturday 16th, but the subsequent two games have unsurprisingly been chosen for TV coverage.

The Reds will now face Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday 24 January at 4:30pm (live on Sky Sports), with the Merseyside derby at Anfield taking place six days later with a 12:30pm kick-off (live on TNT Sports).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The new dates and times for the Man United and Everton games have left Liverpool with a rather difficult week towards the end of January.

Just three days after the game at Old Trafford, the Reds have their concluding fixture in the league phase of the Champions League at home to Lens, and then a turnaround of just over 50 hours to hosting the Toffees at Anfield.

*FA Cup third round draw and fixture details to be confirmed in December

**If Liverpool advance to Carabao Cup semi-finals

The hope is that, by the time the Ligue 1 outfit visit L4 on 27 January, we’ll already be assured of a direct passage to the round of 16 and there won’t be anything riding on that game for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Liverpool currently have seven matches in the diary in the first month of 2027, with an FA Cup third-round tie to be added for the weekend of 9/10 January and a potential Carabao Cup semi-final first leg in the subsequent midweek, should we defeat Bournemouth at Anfield next month.

It’s quite plausible that the Reds could have two matches against Everton in January, with both teams still in the Carabao Cup and favourites to win their respective quarter-finals (the Toffees are away to Fleetwood of League Two).

Three Merseyside derbies in the first five weeks of 2027 would be the definition of familiarity breeding contempt, but for now the sole focus for Iraola and co is the small matter of Man United at home on Sunday.

#1964. Arsenal fan quizzes Graham Scott on why Newcastle United goal not disallowed

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Graham Scott has been quizzed by an Arsenal fan as to why Malick Thiaw’s goal was allowed to stand on Saturday.

That goal put Newcastle United 2-1 up on 62 minutes.

Graham Scott refereed in the Premier League for a decade and he was also a video assistant referee (VAR) more than 100 times.

Now retired, he brings his unique insight into how match officials operate for The Athletic.

They invite readers to send in questions each week for Graham Scott to answer.

This week the former top referee received this one from an Arsenal fan…

‘Why did neither the referee nor VAR penalise the holding on Jurrien Timber that allowed Dan Burn to win a free header to create Newcastle’s second goal against Arsenal?’

Graham Scott explaining: “Timber was impeded by Will Osula as he chased after Burn (circled below). Osula was impeded by Declan Rice, who was holding him with both arms. Malick Thiaw was being held by Martin Odegaard, who was being held by Thiaw. Lewis Miley blocked Ezri Konsa, who pulled Miley to get past him. There were probably other potential fouls, too. The officials look for the most serious offences that have the greatest impact, and none of these came close to meeting those thresholds — which are set by the league and the lawmakers, not the refs.”

I know that no football fan takes it well when any decision goes against them BUT as a group I think Arsenal fans do appear especially bizarre in terms of not willing to accept any decision that doesn’t go their way.

Graham Scott was also asked another question regarding Saturday’s game…

‘When David Raya went down for treatment the first time at Newcastle on Saturday, why did another Arsenal player not have to leave the field for a minute? I thought that was the new rule.’

Graham Scott: ‘No Arsenal player was asked to leave the field for a minute because Raya had collided with an opponent and requested treatment at the earliest opportunity. There is a similar exemption if a goalkeeper’s injury occurs from a foul that the referee deems worthy of a yellow or red card. This rule was introduced to stop goalkeepers mysteriously sitting down and demanding treatment for fictitious muscle injuries while their coach held an impromptu time-out chat with the rest of the team.’

I have to confess, I totally forgot about this new rule coming in. Has any goalkeeper got ‘injured’ this season and had treatment on the pitch which led to his Premier League side going down to ten men for a minute with an outfield player going off?

#1963. Portsmouth 1 – 0 West Ham United | Player ratings as Parker’s team slump to new low

Jarrod Bowen marked his 300th appearance for West Ham at Portsmouth tonight, hoping against hope that the anniversary would be marked by a West Ham win. The Hammers captain hit the post in the opening minutes – and West Ham went behind yet again through their own terrible defending.

West Ham sat eleventh at half time, apparently, so I read, their lowest-ever league position in 131 years*. West Ham came close in the second half as their desperation increased: Shots rattled the bar but the ball stayed out.. and Parker lost again.

Herrick: 3 Portsmouth’s first corner did nothing to settle Herrick’s nerves as his dodgy punch was gratefully cleared. Poor defending for Portsmouth’s goal, Herrick saved the first cross but couldn’t save the shot that led to Portsmouth’s goal. Slightly dodgy fluffed volleyed clearance that the youngster somehow got away with on 40 minutes. Shaky tonight.

Veltman: 3 Put through by Bowen, one delightful chip across the face of Portsmouth’s goal, just agonisingly too high for Piroe to reach. Subbed by Soucek 62′.

Mavropanos: 4 Went down in the opposition box like a shot gazelle where it was arguably a penalty, but his theatrical dive probably convinced the referee otherwise. Came close with a shot late on.

Kilman: 3 First contribution was to be caught in possession after 13 minutes in a dreadful piece of dawdling defending. Fortunately, only a throw-in resulted. Poor defending for Portsmouth’s goal, didn’t close down the right winger and would have at ;east attempted a tackle.

Mayers:  3 Superb pass to put Solomon through on 18 minutes. A torrid evening chasing his winger as West Ham’s fluid defensive shape changed when they pushed for a goal.

Álvarez – 4: Went on one kamikaze run across the whole of his own penalty box and lost possession just outside. Fortunately, Portsmouth couldn’t capitalise.  Looked leggy after two games in three days: Subbed for Magassa on 69′

Engels: – 5 Spent most of the first half predominantly operating down the right-hand side with a couple of useful touches. Hit one curling free kick well but straight at the keeper. Went close when he met Austbø’s cross and headed back across the goal for Souček, but agonisingly inches over the midfielder’s head.

Kanté – 5: Tried and failed to walk the ball into the net after the Portsmouth keeper fluffed his own punch from a corner. One lung-busting run early in the second half resulted in a half chance. Subbed for Castellanos 78′.

Now – familiar sinking feeling after conceding in the first half

Bowen: 4.5 Hit the post in the fourth minute as West Ham’s hoodoo of being unable to score continued. Put Veltman through for his delightful chip across goal. Ineffective in the second half when moved centrally.

Piroe – 3: Agonisingly close on 44 minutes as his scuffed shot was deflected inches wide. Little involvement, no chances created. Anonymous. Subbed by Austbo 62′

Solomon – 2: Put through by a superb pass from Mayers on 18 minutes but decided to check back rather than cross with his weak foot. Constantly reminded me of Saîd Benrahma, always slowing the game by checking inside rather than taking on his full-back. Subbed by Mukasa 69‘.

Souček: 7 A brilliant left-footed drive from the edge of the box which the keeper parried onto the crossbar. Brave header in the dying minutes which was well saved, spilling blood again in the West Ham cause.

Austbø: : 6 Great chance to level it on 81 minutes, but his header was straight at the goalkeeper.

Magassa:  3  Two aimless overhit panic passes, playing as if it was the last minute.

Mukasa: 5 Great work inside the box with a cross for Austbø, but the Norwegian headed it straight at the keeper.

Castellanos: No involvement in his 10 minutes, No rating

#1962. Portsmouth 1 – 0 West Ham United | The morning after

West Ham’s manager Scott Parker, from his demeanour last night, is understandably in a pretty dark place just now after losing his second game in charge, four games now without a win: West Ham now twelfth in the second division with two points from their last eighteen.

“If you are going through hell, keep going” is the oft-quoted popular saying, accredited to Winston Churchill but applicable to just about any circumstance when deep in the smelly stuff.

It’s only football. We understand. But it is supposed to be the very salvation from all of the bad things going on in the world right now.

Which is why it feels pretty lousy being a West Ham fan right now, especially those intrepid away fans who braved the worst of the British transport system and weather to turn up and support their team at Fratton Park.

“The day is darkest just before the dawn” – It was pretty damn’ dark at Fratton Park last night

How long must that journey home have felt, arriving home in the wee small hours replaying a kind of mental lowlights reel – and there were a few lowlights, let’s face it.

Most worrying of all is that the Championship’s top scorers seemingly now cannot put the ball in the back of the net.

However, a sneaky peek at the ‘bookies latest odds suggest they know something we don’t, with West Ham still odds-on (3/10 this morning) to finish in the top six. I’m not a betting man but strip away the emotion (which this ‘morning after’ column is supposed to do ) and there’s still a cold, calculating expectation that someone – presumably Scott Parker – can turn this ship around. There’s still time.

West Ham are the width of a goal post away from fourth place. The season is long and it is not yet December. Get behind whichever eleven are sent out to do battle with Stoke on Saturday. And wait for the dodgy decision in our favour or the outrageous deflected goal that we don’t deserve – which will signal a change of fortunes. COYI!

#1961. One Shot, One Goal, Three Points: West Ham’s Season in a Nutshell

After another disastrous result last night, I was left scratching my head wondering what can actually be done to solve the problems facing West Ham. If results continue along this trajectory, the Hammers could find themselves looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom end of the Championship table rather than fighting for promotion. At this rate, even a play-off spot feels optimistic.

I think 50 points might be enough to survive this league!

Earlier this week I wrote about the statistics, and they tell the real story behind West Ham’s struggles.

Shot after shot, chance after chance, attack after attack, and still the ball refuses to go in. Remarkably, despite their wastefulness, the Hammers remain the division’s top scorers. In the last two matches alone, they have struck the woodwork five times.

Against Portsmouth, West Ham registered 19 shots with six on target and failed to score.

When you add that to the wider picture, the numbers become even more alarming. Across the last six matches, West Ham have taken 130 shots, with 41 on target, and scored only eight goals.

At the opposite end of the pitch, defensive frailties and questionable goalkeeping continue to cost the team. Herrick was barely tested at Fratton Park, but when he was called into action, he was beaten. The goal will almost certainly be recorded as a goalkeeping error. Portsmouth created virtually nothing, yet their only shot on target produced the winning goal.

You can only work with the players available, but it’s difficult to understand how Areola has suffered multiple injuries this season despite not playing a competitive match. Entering the final year of his contract, albeit with a club option for an additional season, he is reportedly earning around £60,000 per week.

These are issues that might be understandable in the Premier League. This is the Championship. These players, including the youngsters, should be capable of performing consistently at this level.

Heads – down, negativity growing…time to stop the rot…

The negativity around the club is beginning to grow.

Nuno had to go, and he did. His departure gave Parker an opportunity to reintegrate certain players and rebuild fitness levels through competitive football. To be fair, time has not always been on the new manager’s side. However, following the international break, he has now had a chance to work with the squad, implement his ideas and stamp his authority on the team.

The last two matches have to fall at his door. One point from six is simply not good enough. Extend that across his first four games and the record reads two defeats and two draws.

The much-talked-about new manager bounce? It never arrived.

You can see the frustration written all over the players’ faces. The supporters are becoming restless too, and I include myself in that group. I predicted a narrow 1-0 victory for West Ham at Portsmouth, but deep down I feared a repeat of the Preston performance. Unfortunately, those fears proved worse as at least we got a point on Saturday!

Against Preston, West Ham enjoyed 80% possession and recorded 53 touches inside the opposition penalty area. Preston registered just ten.

At Fratton Park, the Hammers dominated possession with 63% of the ball and managed 29 touches in Portsmouth’s box compared to just eight for the home side.

At this point, I’m running out of explanations. The statistics suggest West Ham should be winning games comfortably, but football is decided by goals, not data. Right now, the Hammers can’t convert their dominance into results, and until that changes, the gap between expectation and reality will continue to grow. I’m lost for words. I really am!

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

Select your team accordingly (no Solomon for instance and Austbo told to speed it up). . In midfield, move the ball quickly and forwards, with incisive passes. #1960. Liverpool ‘showing concrete interest’ in Bundesliga wonderkid Jurgen Klopp likes

Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.

The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.

The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.

Christian Falk told CF Bayern Insider: “However, Bayern Munich definitely have him on the list. And we should note that both Liverpool and Brighton in the Premier League are showing concrete interest in the 17-year-old attacking talent.

“This is why Gladbach would be well-advised to try and offer him a new contract; that way, they can have some influence over how long the player stays at the club, or, at the very least, ensure that they get a sizeable sum from a permanent transfer.

“I heard that there has already been contact with Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and they talked about a move to Leverkusen. The next step is to talk to the player, his family and then the club. He doesn’t have a long-term contract at Gladbach, so there is a chance to make this deal happen.”

With a contract currently set to expire in the summer of 2028, Mohya represents a genuine market opportunity for clubs looking to invest in a high-potential option.

On that note, Brighton makes a great deal of sense as the next stop in the 17-year-old’s career (if not his final destination), similarly to Leverkusen in the German top-flight.

Liverpool, it has to be said, would benefit greatly from a player with the Gladbach star’s profile, given they lack a viable backup option to Florian Wirtz in the ten position. Not to mention the fact that the footballer would provide further reassurance on the flanks.

Falk went on to add: “The 17-year-old was invited to the national team by Klopp during the international break. He wasn’t officially part of the squad; it was more just to give the player a taste of what international football looks like. He’s not totally clear yet about where he wants to commit, but Germany is putting up a strong fight to ensure that he pledges his international future to Die Nationalelf.”

The big issue facing Mohya in the coming weeks and months, of course, is whether a move to the likes of FC Bayern and Liverpool are actually in his best interest at this stage in his career.

Bayern Munich have Ismael Saibari and Jamal Musiala behind Harry Kane, albeit there are question marks over the latter’s long-term future in Munich in light of ongoing concerns over his health.

The Reds, of course, have Wirtz, in whom they invested a British transfer record fee (the total package being worth £116.5m). He’s played a significant percentage of the total minutes on offer in 2026/27 under new boss Andoni Iraola, and at 23 years of age, he’s hardly at any risk of sinking past his peak in the near future.

We’ve no doubt Liverpool would welcome having a rotational option of Mohya’s quality, whom they could develop on their own time, and they can supply evidence of how well they’re managing Rio Ngumoha’s development despite the presence of more senior figures in Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo.

But if Wael Mohya’s looking for an absolute guarantee of regular minutes, you could forgive him for either staying put in Germany or joining the talent factory line in Brighton.

#1959. Scott Parker damns his own players with this painful one-word home truth | West Ham News

Scott Parker could do little else other than state the obvious last night as West Ham plumbed new depths of mediocrity against their south coast opponents. For the first time this season, the league’s top scorers failed to find their opponent’s net despite again hitting the woodwork twice.

Speaking after the game, Parker came up with a new expression for ‘pulling their finger out’ – when speaking to West Ham tv:

“We need to fix up as a group and as a team and give ourselves a platform.”

This is an honest group. They’re probably too desperate, really and I think that’s weighing quite heavy and you can see that.

it’s just certain moments we’re a little bit soft in certain moments. We’re easy to play against in certain moments.”

Which means, as we can all see for ourselves it is less about the quality of the play, more about the mental resilience of the eleven on the pitch who have seemingly lost – for the time being – the ability to take another low blow and fight back. Conceding one goal away at Portsmouth is no disaster. Failing to register two goals against them is the real failing.

Another year, another hit: Soucek’s commitment to this team stands head, shoulders, torso and boots above some within the limp lettuce line up. Right now it ss more about the character of those selected than the ability.

At times earlier in the season West Ham would have romped down the other end and banged in three in quick succession to redress the balance and grab the points. And that is what Parker needs to find again. It isn’t the magic fix of a ‘perfect’ defensive performance, our players aren’t good enough to give us that. It is a mental resilience that ten didn’t have last night.

Eleven Tomas Souceks, players who are prepared to bleed for this club, will do nicely.

Clearly some ( c’mon, we know who they are) aren’t prepared to dig in, to battle, to die for the shirt ( metaphorically speaking of course) ands they’re the ones who need to be sidelined. Forget the (huh) best footballers. Give us 10 fighters alongside Soucek.

The Czech showed again why, without being the best footballer, he wins the admiration of every West Ham fan. Because he bleeds for the team. The rest would do well to follow his example.

Copyright issues prevent me showing the image of Soucek lying prostrate after another whack in the face last night. Go Google.

#1958. Saudi Arabia PIF have now put 25 per cent of Newcastle United up for sale

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Breaking news on Wednesday that the Saudi Arabia PIF have put 25 per cent of Newcastle United up for sale.

The exclusive comes from David Ornstein and Chris Waugh at The Athletic.

They reveal that this would be done through the issuing of new shares.

The Athletic stating: ‘The proposed transaction would see new investors inject funds directly into the club, receiving up to a quarter shareholding in exchange. No funds would flow to PIF, but its existing stake would be diluted by the share issue.’

They add that JP Morgan (the New York City-headquartered global bank) has been appointed advisors and that the process to find investment is under way.

The Athletic journalists detailing: ‘Sources with knowledge of the situation, speaking on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to do so publicly, insisted that, at this point, a minority investor is being sought with PIF eager to raise money, in part to fund major infrastructure projects, and regard the issuing of new shares as a good means of doing so.’

It appears that the 25 per cent of the total shareholding to be sold will come from the 84 per cent of the club owned by the Saudi Arabia PIF, as the report adds that: ‘The British Reuben family owns the remaining 16 per cent shareholding and Jamie Reuben is their representative on the board.’

Back in May 2026, The Athletic had previously reported that the Newcastle United majority owners were open to selling a minority stake to help fund significant infrastructure projects: ‘However, people familiar with the matter insisted PIF retained a long-term commitment to the club they jointly bought from Mike Ashley for a total of £305million ($400.1m at present exchange rates) in 2021, though they were willing to dilute their shareholding and had already been approached by possible investors. Yasir Al-Rumayyan, PIF’s governor and Newcastle’s chairman, attended his first match of the season at St James’ Park on Saturday, watching Newcastle draw 2-2 with league champions Arsenal. Jamie Reuben was also at the match.’

This news today will hopefully signal plans for the new stadium set to finally go head, as well as the new state of the art training ground.

The Athletic adding: ‘While PIF was never going to pay for a new stadium outright — Newcastle have always been viewed as a long-term investment intended to bring them an eventual profit — any project of that scale would require a notable injection of equity as well as outside financing.’
